_note: What is under the lake, and the same map twice. Entered before the Drambus Stack comes down it is flooded: the two middle rows are water, the west stair is shut, and the only way to the bottom is the long way round the slag — twenty-one tiles at two hundred and sixty per mille instead of eleven at thirty. Entered after, `drains` turns the water to bed and the straight run down the middle opens. Same boss, same loadout, same drop; what the early way costs is the walk, which is the only currency a dungeon here has. Not a second boss and not a second map — one of each, read twice.

places.name: the two hundred and six steps
the bottom of the lake
prose: It stops, and the noise it was making stops with it, and what is left is water moving somewhere you cannot see.
Behind it the wall is not a wall. It is a door, and it has been a door the whole time, and there are eleven inches of silt banked against the bottom of it that nobody has swept.

places.name: the door under the lake
prose: The silt comes away in one piece, the way a thing does when it has been there long enough to have set, and the door opens inwards on four hinges of which two are original.
Behind it is a landing and a stair going down, cut for people carrying something, and the stair does not stop where the light does.
This is where the writing stops. Not the game — the writing. What is at the bottom of that stair is not hidden and not locked and not saved for later: nobody has decided it yet.
You dropped a tower, drained a lake and walked two hundred and six steps into the dark, and the last fact this game has for you is that somebody cut them.
